title: Screening and Intelligence-led Measures to Identify Visa-exempt Visitors Intending to Engage in Vice-related Activities
what_it_is: Screening and Intelligence-led Measures to Identify Visa-exempt Visitors Intending to Engage in Vice-related Activities

sections.label: ICA pre-arrival risk assessments
sections.summary: ICA uses data analytics, advance passenger information and No-Boarding Directives to identify and scrutinise higher-risk travellers before granting entry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Home Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) leverages data analytics to conduct pre-arrival risk assessments using advance passenger information, intelligence, watchlists and other available information to identify travellers of interest or other factors, such as patterns of travel, that may warrant further scrutiny.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Home Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Travellers arriving at our checkpoints who are assessed or profiled to present a higher risk will also be subjected to further interviews and checks, before ICA determines whether to grant them entry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Home Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In January this year, ICA introduced a new upstream measure by issuing No-Boarding Directive (NBD) notices to airlines operators at Changi and Seletar Airports, which requires the operators to prevent persons identified as prohibited or undesirable travellers from boarding flights bound for Singapore.

sections.label: Foreigners refused entry at checkpoints
sections.summary: Foreigners intending vice-related activities are deemed undesirable, and about 45,000 visitors were refused entry in 2025, up 38.3% from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Foreigners seeking entry into Singapore and who are assessed to have the intention to engage in vice-related activities in Singapore will be deemed as undesirable persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Having said that, the ICA does not track those foreigners who are on visa-free entry and who are engaging in illegal activities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In 2025, approximately about 45,000 foreign visitors were refused entry at Singapore's checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: This represents about a 38.3% increase from around 33,000 foreign visitors who were denied entry in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: These foreigners were assessed to pose immigration or security risks, or believed to have the intention to come to Singapore to work illegally.
